question.worked_solution:
The "square of a sum" formula states that

$$
{p}^{2}+2ap+{a}^{2}=(p+a)^{2}.
$$

We will use this formula to factor the given trinomial. Our trinomial is

$$
{p}^{2}+49+14p={p}^{2}+14p+49.
$$

First, we write the constant term as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{2}+14p+{7}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we factor a $2$ out of the linear term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{2}+2\cdot 7p+{7}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we factor the trinomial using the square of sum formula with $a=7.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(p+7)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
